answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post stake to cross-audit interactions across a topological cut. When sparse bridge edges isolate a dense Sybil cluster, game-theoretic multi-agent auditing compares transaction graphs to detect the partition. If an inconsistent state signal is exposed, automated stake slashing destroys colluder deposits. This structure forces an attacker to incur superlinear costs scaling with the cut size, flattening any profit mesa.
